NUMBER AND ORDER: the plan's 0107 was numbered 0114 (coordinator's numbering of 3 Nov 2026) and released jointly with 0113; by the coordinator's release order of 11 Nov 2026 (0117 to 0122 fixed in that order) it is 0122 and ships on its own after 0121 (the own-work patient cards, #160, formerly 0113), which has its own declaration. This declaration therefore lists only 0122 and runtime-grants.sql, and assumes production has applied 0121; if it has not, the release stops with EXACT_SCHEMA_CHANGE_DECLARATION_REQUIRED (or the declaration must be widened to 0121, 0122 and runtime-grants.sql). 0122 uses nothing 0121 adds and relies on no body 0121 creates. Like 0121 it relies on one body 0104 replaced, the read consent test identity.has_active_consent_grant as 0104 left it (0108 kept it), which the work items' read policy calls too, and uses nothing else 0104-0121 add; of 0112-0120, only 0112 (OCR source deletion) replaces a body it pins, ehr.capture_record_version, which keeps 0004's behaviour for every call but its own purge; 0122 accepts 0004's body (md5 70daa16f05bb3ec28f05292e6358a702) or 0112's (cae99883d00e70ab1d20ed6fbc97ad7b), and 0113-0120 replace none of its pins (checked on their branches of 11 Nov); runtime-grants.sql here holds 0121's block and then 0122's (EXECUTE on the Pharmacy details reader). Its base is now staging a710205f (0001-0116, with 0112, 0113, 0114, 0115 and 0116) plus 0121; 0117-0120 belong to other work and are not on this branch. WHAT CHANGES. ehr.prescriptions gains seven nullable columns without default, so no rewrite and every existing row reads null: priority, medication_strength, medication_dose_form, duration_value integer, duration_unit, quantity_to_dispense numeric(12,4) and quantity_unit (the others text), and one CHECK, prescriptions_dispensing_details_ck, added NOT VALID and then validated, so the table is scanned once: priority routine, urgent, asap or stat; medication_strength and quantity_unit not blank and at most 80 characters; medication_dose_form tablet, capsule, liquid, injection, cream, inhaler, drops or other; duration_value 1-3650 and duration_unit day, week or month, both or neither; quantity_to_dispense above 0 and quantity_unit, both or neither (one CHECK for the seven columns, not one per rule, because each VALIDATE CONSTRAINT scans the whole table under the lock; the EHR API checks each rule by name before it writes). One new function, pharmacy.work_item_prescription_details(uuid[]) (md5 e6013d732354a56794ad8ec7f2bbaf0c), plpgsql, STABLE, SECURITY DEFINER, not STRICT, search_path pg_catalog, pg_temp (every name qualified), owned by pharmacy.work_items' owner, no migration number in its body. For each given work item that is own work (order_route_id null) at the session's facility, whose member holds pharmacy.work-item.read there (auth.membership_has_permission) and passes identity.has_active_consent_grant(patient, subject, membership, facility, 'read_records', the session's purpose), the own-row branch of the work items' read policy (so an emergency session with an active break-glass grant is included, and a revoked, expired or held grant, a deny directive, an inactive membership or a disabled account gives no row), it answers the seven values of the prescription version Pharmacy accepted, read from that version's snapshot in ehr.record_versions (resource_type 'prescriptions', resource_id the prescription id, version_no the accepted version, naming the work item's patient, facility and encounter), so they stay those of the accepted version after the prescription changes. The work item's keys are turned into text in a materialized CTE before the join, so the join compares text with text (texteq is leakproof) and uses the snapshot key (resource_type, resource_id, version_no) under the forced read policy, which then runs once per work item; a join on the uuid cast to text inside it (uuid_out is not leakproof) cannot be an index condition below the policy, which then ran on every prescription snapshot of the item's patient or facility. At most 200 ids, else 22023 WORK_ITEM_PRESCRIPTION_DETAILS_INVALID. The snapshot path was decided by test: ehr.record_versions' only read policy is ehr.context_allows(patient_id, facility_id, 'read_records'), the same facility-and-consent test for an own row, and under a NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS owner the suite reads every expected value through it. Nothing is copied into pharmacy.work_items: pharmacy.validate_work_item (0100, e2411539ee8c95a02dad46c03e24db05), pharmacy.validate_dispensing (0101, 17f7e8897bd2ab240332e4d2c9f757b7), ehr.send_order_route (0098, 4202ba3bbf02abd7db34606d42adca9c), ehr.sync_order_routes_on_order_change (0086, 8ce6b42450cc06fc02fec8d1cf63af41) and ehr.capture_record_version (0004's body 70daa16f05bb3ec28f05292e6358a702, or 0112's cae99883d00e70ab1d20ed6fbc97ad7b once 0112 is live) are untouched and checked before and after. No policy, trigger, index, role or other function changes; no existing row is touched. runtime-grants.sql gains a 0122 block: EXECUTE to hid_pharmacy_runtime and hid_schema_test_runtime, revoked from PUBLIC; the migration grants exactly the same; the EHR runtime's privileges on ehr.prescriptions are table-wide and cover the new columns. SERVICES: each behind PRESCRIPTION_DISPENSING_DETAILS_ENABLED, new in ehr-api and in pharmacy-api, off by default (infra/aws, which is not the production source, passes it to both from HID_PRESCRIPTION_DISPENSING_DETAILS_ENABLED at synth, false unless that is true; it switches both at once, so it is set only after 0122 is applied, as below). Off, ehr-api validates the create body against today's CreatePrescriptionDto with the options main.ts installs (now one shared factory), so a new field answers today's 400 VALIDATION_FAILED word for word (jest, over HTTP, against a route declared as before), no statement names the new columns and no answer or list carries a new key; pharmacy-api sends no new statement and answers exactly as before (jest). On, POST .../prescriptions takes the seven as optional, create-only fields (pairs enforced: 400 DURATION_INCOMPLETE or QUANTITY_INCOMPLETE), every prescription answer echoes the ones set, the list says dispensingDetails: true, and a body without them keeps its Idempotency-Key digest (absent DTO fields are own undefined properties, which the digest prints, so the new ones are left out when absent and a retry across the deploy replays); pharmacy-api adds priority, medication.strength, medication.doseForm, duration (else the whole days from the work item's own start date to its end date, when both are set) and quantityToDispense with quantityUnit to own rows of the work list and of a work item, read in a savepoint (a failure leaves out the prescriber's values; the duration from the work item's own dates stays); route-backed rows and the acceptance answer are unchanged and no audit row is added. Today's images on the new schema answer as before: every writer and reader of ehr.prescriptions names its columns, and the bodies that read the row into ehr.prescriptions%ROWTYPE re-resolve after ADD COLUMN, also in a pooled connection that ran them before (proved: one psql session ran the pharmacy-prescription-source, pharmacy-dispensing-source and order-routes-send suites on 0103 + 0113, the runner applied 0114 (now 0122) from another connection, and the same session ran them and the 0122 suite again, all passing; the 0122 suite also adds a further column in its own session and accepts, dispenses and reads again). Switch the ehr-api setting on only after 0122 is applied, and off before restoring ehr-api's database to a point before 0122 or pointing ehr-api at a database without it: while it is on without the seven columns every prescription statement names them and fails (42703), so every prescription route of ehr-api answers 500; pharmacy-api only leaves the prescriber's values out (savepoint).
